summary.text: A 72-year-old female with past hypertension and depression, an ex-smoker who stopped four years ago and denied sunbed use or excessive sun exposure, was referred to plastic surgery with a three-month history of sudden growth of a longstanding pigmented lesion on the medial aspect of her left knee. Examination showed a 2 x 1cm raised, nodular, pigmented lesion, and an excision biopsy was performed because melanoma was suspected.

The excised nodule was well-circumscribed, 12 x 10 x 8mm, with an adjacent 7 x 6mm light brown plaque. Microscopy showed a single lesion with two distinct components: an invasive superficial spreading melanoma with a Breslow thickness of 3.0mm and no ulceration, and a central dermal nodule of osteoclast-like giant cells and atypical mononuclear cells with marked pleomorphism and a high mitotic count.

On immunohistochemistry the melanoma component was positive for Melan A and SOX-10 while the central nodule was negative for them. The nodule was positive for CD 10, CD 68 and CD 163 with a high Ki-67 proliferation index, and negative for S100, HMB-45, the cytokeratins, p63 and smooth muscle actin. It was diagnosed as AFX. BRAF analysis found no codon 600 mutation in the melanoma component.

The pathological melanoma stage was pT3a (AJCC 8) with clinical stage 2A, and both the nodule and the melanoma were well excised. Subsequently, wide local excision of the surgical scar showed scarring only, and sentinel lymph node biopsy of two left groin nodes found both benign. After discussion at the Melanoma Multidisciplinary meeting, a treatment and follow-up plan was put in place.

article_limitations: Single case; no post-treatment outcome, recurrence status or follow-up result is stated.
No dates are given; the order of excision biopsy, histology, BRAF analysis, wide local excision with sentinel node biopsy and the multidisciplinary discussion is only partly stated.

The clinical lesion size (2 x 1cm) and the macroscopic nodule (12 x 10 x 8mm) and adjacent plaque (7 x 6mm) sizes are separate measurements; the source does not relate them, and they are not treated as a conflict.
Discussion statements about AFX and melanoma in general and about the cited cases are literature background, not facts about this patient.
Figure panels were inspected in the separate visual submission; caption-layer visual status stays not_inspected.

The negated disjunction "denied any sunbed use or excessive sun exposure" is recorded as two absent exposures (a denial covers each alternative); this differs from an affirmative "X or Y", which asserts neither.
The multidisciplinary meeting and plan are stated only in the Conclusions and are not ordered against the wide local excision or sentinel node biopsy.
